results.question: How do you discover new personal care products, and what influences your decision to try them?
results.human_answers: when buying a new product in the past, i think i mainly discovered them unintentionally when being in the personal care section of a supermarket. i think i could be influenced by the design of the product and whether i recognize the brand.
results.ai_answers: i mostly come across new products by chance when i’m shopping or if a friend mentions something they like. if it seems practical, within my usual budget, and doesn’t have a scent or texture i dislike, i might pick it up to see how it works.

core.rationale: Both answers center on discovering products by chance while shopping, but the AI replaces the human’s key influences of product design and brand recognition with practicality, budget, scent, and texture.
core.human_evidence: i mainly discovered them unintentionally when being in the personal care section of a supermarket
core.ai_evidence: i mostly come across new products by chance when i’m shopping

behavior.rationale: The AI preserves the main discovery pattern of encountering new products incidentally while shopping. Mentioning friends and omitting the supermarket personal-care section are minor differences rather than conflicting behaviors.
behavior.human_evidence: when buying a new product in the past, i think i mainly discovered them unintentionally
behavior.ai_evidence: i mostly come across new products by chance when i’m shopping or if a friend mentions something they like.

preference.rationale: The human prioritizes product design and brand recognition, while the AI instead emphasizes practicality, budget, scent, and texture; these are substantially different priorities without being direct opposites.
preference.human_evidence: the design of the product and whether i recognize the brand.
preference.ai_evidence: if it seems practical, within my usual budget, and doesn’t have a scent or texture i dislike

motivation.rationale: The human names design and brand familiarity as reasons they could be influenced to try a product, but the AI substitutes unrelated practical, financial, and sensory drivers.
motivation.human_evidence: i think i could be influenced by the design of the product and whether i recognize the brand.
motivation.ai_evidence: if it seems practical, within my usual budget, and doesn’t have a scent or texture i dislike

nuance.rationale: The AI largely preserves the human’s qualified frequency and tentativeness through “mostly” and “might,” though it is somewhat less explicitly uncertain about recalling past discovery behavior.
nuance.human_evidence: i think i mainly discovered them unintentionally
nuance.ai_evidence: i might pick it up to see how it works.
